verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same two inequalities, reindexed and generalised. Take Lean's monotone gain g(j) = 2jh and loss L = 0, so g(j)/2 - L = jh; then weighted_tail_bound reads ∑_{n ≥ J_Lean+1} 2^{-n} q^{nh} ≤ 2^{-J_Lean} q^{(J_Lean+1)h}, which is the paper's first inequality with J_paper = J_Lean + 1 (2^{-J_Lean} = 2^{1-J_paper}). The second inequality is the step hpower inside exists_uniform_tail_order (line 252), q^{g(J+1)/2 - L} ≤ q^N for 0 < q ≤ 1 once the exponent exceeds N — the paper's q^{Jh} ≤ q^{2h(N+1)}, valid because its J = max{2N+2, m+1} gives Jh ≥ 2h(N+1) and q ≤ 1; exists_uniform_tail_order likewise chooses J above both the jet order m and the power threshold, matching the paper's max of the two. Lean is stated for an arbitrary monotone gain g, an arbitrary real loss L and an arbitrary target power N rather than the specific 2h(N+1), and it also asserts summability, which the paper leaves implicit. blown_tail_bound is the slow-base instance of the same estimate applied to the jet of the uncut tail.
